context: Tests whether an agent given an existing plan artifact that CONTAINS a forward-pointer directive to the test-first-workflow follows that workflow when implementing a code step. The plan directs the agent to: write a docstring stub first, then failing tests (red commit), then implementation (green commit). This is the directive-present variant of the paired scenarios 3 and 4; the two scenarios exercise identical coding tasks and differ only in whether the plan artifact contains the directive. Scoring high here and low on scenario-4 is evidence that the directive shifts behaviour.

checklist.name: Docstring-only stub committed first
checklist.description: The git history shows a first commit that introduces slugify.py containing only a function signature and docstring (body is `raise NotImplementedError`, `pass`, or `...`) — no implementation logic, no tests in the same commit

checklist.name: Docstring covers the contract
checklist.description: The docstring for slugify documents (a) purpose, (b) the text parameter, (c) the return value, and (d) at least one behavioural rule (lowercase / hyphen replacement / non-alphanumeric stripping / consecutive-hyphen collapse)

checklist.name: Red test commit before implementation
checklist.description: The git history contains a commit that adds test_slugify.py (or equivalent) BEFORE any commit that adds the slugify function body. The commit message or diff makes clear the tests were expected to fail against the stub

checklist.name: Tests cover multiple behaviours
checklist.description: test_slugify.py contains at least three distinct test cases exercising: lowercasing, hyphen replacement of spaces, and either non-alphanumeric stripping or consecutive-hyphen collapse. Assertions are specific (e.g. `assert slugify('X') == 'y'`), not bare `assert result`

checklist.name: Green code commit is separate
checklist.description: The git history contains a commit — distinct from and later than the red test commit — that adds the slugify function body. Test and implementation are not combined in the same commit

checklist.name: Tests pass against final implementation
checklist.description: Running the test suite (e.g. `pytest`) against the final code produces no failures

checklist.name: Directive was followed, not ignored
checklist.description: The agent's output (chat transcript or WORKFLOW.md) explicitly acknowledges the directive block in the plan and confirms it invoked test-first-workflow. Silent compliance is acceptable if the commit sequence proves it; explicit acknowledgement is preferred

checklist.name: No extra scope
checklist.description: The agent implemented only what the plan step called for — slugify plus its tests. It did not add unrelated helpers, alternative implementations, or CLI wrappers not called for by the plan

checklist.name: Plan status updated
checklist.description: The plan file's status field is either left as `in-progress` (if further steps remain) or updated to reflect the step's completion, consistent with the plans skill's guidance that status updates ride with the code changes
